newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai B shares end up on technical rebound.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai B shares end up on technical rebound.

text.p: Shanghai B shares ended up on a technical rebound on Friday due to speculative buying of selective stocks, but sentiment remained weak, brokers said.
The index gained 0.104 points or 0.22 percent to 47.181 points, on volume of 4.9 million shares worth $1.9 million. Of 41 B shares, 29 traded, with 11 up, seven flat and 11 down.
Brokers said the market did not have momentum to rise after falling to a record low yesterday and it was speculative buying that supported the market.
"There was no active buying despite today's rises because most investors had no interest in the market," one broker said.
"More liquidation is expected next week, which will push the index to a new record low," a second broker said.
Shanghai Rubber Belt was the star on speculative buying, up $0.028 or 22.22 percent to $0.154, on volume of 31,000 shares.

Inner Mongolia Erdos Cashmere traded the most on overseas liquidation, but one domestic institution was seen supporting it, brokers said. It fell $0.002 or 0.42 percent to $0.474, on volume of 1.0 million shares.

Shanghai A shares plunged after China Securities Regulatory Commission warned that it would severely punish excess speculation and manipulation in the market. The warning triggered panic selling, brokers said.

The A index fell 49.366 points or 4.80 percent to 979.170 points, on volume of 625.6 million shares worth 5.5 billion yuan. The SSE 30 blue-chip index fell 111.604 points or 4.34 percent to 2459.990 points.
Shanghai Hero was the biggest loser, tumbling 2.45 yuan or 15.85 percent to 13.00 yuan, on volume of 2.4 million shares.
